propositions: A detached sweep worker that dies between rename and commit leaves the tracker working tree dirty with tracked deletions and untracked snapshot/retired files, causing subsequent reconverge merges to abort and strand commits.

The fold must be crash-atomic by writing an intent journal before mutation, performing ordered snapshot-write/rename/commit with rollback on failure, and scanning for abandoned journals at sweep startup to discriminate landed vs. partial vs. superseded folds.
Recovery must retain uncommitted snapshots on incomplete rollback (to prevent event loss) and discriminate transient git faults from permanent snapshot absence to avoid reverting landed folds.
An intent journal write failure must cause the fold to refuse with exit 1 and zero mutations; journal cleanup must occur in the same locked scope as the fold.
Crash-injection tests must confirm that a fold killed at any step boundary converges to a clean tree (empty git status --porcelain) with no lost events on next sweep entry.
